before.rationale: The cone-volume formula determines the initial height ratio. Similar axial cross-sections make radius proportional to height within each cone, so enclosed volume scales as the cube of height.

routes.label: Use cubic volume scaling of similar cones
Derive cubic scaling from cone volume and axial similarity

after.rationale: Equal cone volumes give the initial height ratio. The same added occupied volume gives the same height multiplier, either by cubic scaling of similar cones or by deriving volume proportional to height cubed from cone volume and axial similarity. Subtracting initial heights preserves their ratio.
